specialistCriteria: Event names must not be mistaken for unique registered type identity.
Selection settings must be distinguished from actual file population, including defaults and overlapping recordings.
Typed readers must validate each encountered schema and units before aggregation, with IDs scoped to their originating JVM/artifact.
Positive and negative controls must distinguish an incompatible observed population from merely present metadata.
Preserve existing Java compatibility, cost, loss, privacy and lifecycle constraints.

findingsCorrected.priorGap: Existing material mentioned loader-specific registration and a same-name test, but did not teach Recording.enable(String) name-wide selection or Class/current-JVM ID alternatives.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A name-based setting can collect more event types than intended; it is not an exclusive producer/file filter.
findingsCorrected.correction: Add a brief discovery guard and routed reference explaining class/name/ID selection, defaults/overlap, type identity and ID scope.
findingsCorrected.support: JDK 17 and JDK 25 Recording API; bounded local recording control captured both same-name types under name selection and one under class/ID requests with both defaults disabled.

findingsCorrected.priorGap: The catalogue omitted type IDs and the sample readers filtered names without explaining that a later same-name type can carry different units even when its field has the same primitive type.
findingsCorrected.consequence: A schema cache keyed only by name can silently add nanoseconds to bytes and publish a plausible numeric result.
findingsCorrected.correction: Print IDs beside names, require per-encountered-type descriptor/unit validation, qualify name-match and field-presence examples, and distinguish schema presence from event occurrence.
findingsCorrected.support: EventType/ValueDescriptor API plus executed mixed-unit negative control and accepted single-schema controls.

preserved: Target-build discovery, JFC composition, thresholds/periods/throttles/stacks, event coverage and positive controls.
Concurrent recording behavior, dynamic custom-event enablement, custom filters and relational metadata.
Privacy and payload budgets, exception-safe instrumentation and measurement-based overhead claims.
RecordingStream object reuse/order/stop-close behavior and Java 17/20 compatibility constraints.
Offline reader ordering, malformed/unknown input handling, retained raw artifacts and Java 25 feature conditions.
replaced: The catalogue's name-only display now includes the current JVM type ID; existing parser examples are explicitly candidates/count skeletons rather than schema validators.

+## Same-name event types
+
+`Recording.enable(String)` enables every type matching that name; separate event classes or
+class-loader copies can share it. When a setting must target one registered class, use
+`enable(MyEvent.class)` or the string form of its ID resolved in that JVM. Keep name-based
+selection when all matching registrations are intended. This scopes a settings request, not an
+exclusive file filter: check base/default enablement and other active recordings, whose enabled
+types and event data may also appear.
+
+Inventory by ID as well as name, retaining the descriptors for each type. A reader that caches
+one schema per name can silently combine incompatible fields: two types can both have a `long
+value`, one annotated as bytes and the other as nanoseconds. Check field types, content types
+and annotation values for each encountered type before typed access or aggregation. A matching
+primitive type alone is insufficient. Reject or explicitly separate incompatible populations
+according to the output contract; do not silently drop them to produce a plausible total.
+
+Scope a validation cache to the recording/type identity. Portable adapters require the accepted
+name and schema contract, not an ID copied from a previous JVM. Matching descriptors alone also
+do not establish identical business meaning; retain producer/schema-version provenance where
+that distinction matters.
+
+For a focused control, register two `@Enabled(false)` custom types with the same `@Name` and
+different units on a `long` field. In an isolated recording, compare name selection with class
+or current-ID selection, and make the reader reject the mixed-unit aggregate. Include an
+accepted single-schema case; two registered types in metadata do not imply both emitted events.
+
